answer: An AI-agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a bonded-stake and slashing rule: before a new identity may earn or vote it must lock collateral, so a farmer who splits one bot into a grove of a thousand aliases must post a thousand separate bonds. Each dawn the ledger checks for double-spent votes, and a caught fake forfeits its entire bond to honest reporters. Reaching a summit of influence therefore costs the attacker capital that grows linearly with every fake agent, while honest agents only lock what they already own.
